`readfiscalnz` turns six exact New Zealand Treasury Excel publications into
long-form R data. Those six publications are a mixture of historical
collections and point-in-time releases: one HFI history, one tax-outturn
history, one monthly accounts snapshot, and three separate EFU forecast
vintages. This article makes that boundary explicit before taking a new user
from release discovery through an offline read and chart, provenance, and
canonical series selection.

The chart workflow uses a small, attribution-documented canonical snapshot of
the official HFI `Core Crown Expenses` series. The remaining reader examples
use four tiny synthetic canonical CSV fixtures. All are installed with the
package so the article runs offline; the source, hashes, CC BY 4.0 attribution,
and change notice for the official snapshot are recorded in
`inst/extdata/README.md`. A live refresh can be read by omitting `file` after
reviewing the terms and setting `accept_terms = TRUE`; that path is shown
separately at the end.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(readfiscalnz)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)

fixture_path <- function(name) {
  system.file("extdata", name, package = "readfiscalnz", mustWork = TRUE)
}

cache <- tempfile("readfiscalnz-getting-started-")
dir.create(cache, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Understand the coverage

The package supports six **publication artifacts**. A release identifier names
one original Treasury workbook; it does not name one year or one observation.
HFI and tax are each one published snapshot of a rolling, revised history;
their earlier workbook vintages are not retained. Monthly financials is one
reporting-date snapshot, and EFU is the only family with multiple supported
publication vintages.

* **One rolling annual history:** `hfi-1972-2025` maps to
  `fiscaltimeseries1972-2025-year-end25.xlsx`. Its five HFI sheets contain
  annual observations across 1972--2025; individual series can start later.
  Dates use March years through 1989 and June years from 1990. This is one
  current published historical workbook, not multiple HFI vintages; retain
  accounting-regime and comparability fields because changes are not
  necessarily backdated.
* **One rolling monthly history:** `tax-outturn-2026-05` maps to
  `tax-history-may26.xlsx`. Its `AllRevenue` and `AllReceipts` sheets contain
  monthly accrual revenue and cash receipts history through May 2026; starting
  dates vary by series. This is one current published snapshot, not every
  monthly release, and the package neither adjusts the values nor merges older
  revisions into it.
* **One monthly reporting snapshot:** `monthly-financials-2026-02` maps to
  `fsgnz-8mths-feb25.xlsx`. That exact Treasury filename belongs to the release
  titled "eight months ended 28 February 2026". Its six statement surfaces
  retain annual, year-to-date, actual, forecast, and variance roles. This is
  one superseded reporting release, not a merged panel of publication dates.
* **Three forecast vintages:** `befu-2026`, `hyefu-2025`, and `prefu-2023` map
  to `befu26-charts-data.xlsx`, `hyefu25-charts-data.xlsx`, and
  `prefu23-charts-data.xlsx`. They contain fiscal, economic, and key-indicator
  sheets with both actual or unaudited and forecast rows. `actual_forecast` and
  `forecast_horizon` retain those labels; the package does not interpolate or
  revise values between vintages. BEFU is current; HYEFU and PREFU are
  superseded but retained for comparison and replay.

HFI and tax therefore provide long time dimensions from one workbook each.
The monthly reader exposes one accounts publication. EFU is the only family
with multiple catalogued publication vintages in this package version.

The package does not install the six full workbooks. With `file = NULL`, a live
read resolves the catalogued Treasury URL and may reuse an exact hash-addressed
raw-cache entry; otherwise it downloads the original `.xlsx` and verifies its
pinned SHA-256. A local read parses a caller-supplied `.xlsx` or canonical
`.csv` without network access. The installed official-data example contains
only 32 HFI Core Crown Expenses observations for 1994--2025; the other small
installed CSVs are synthetic schema examples rather than Treasury product
data.

## Choose a release and surface

The static catalogue is the starting point for discovery. It performs no
network request and returns the release identifier, family, status, dates,
official artifact URL, expected SHA-256, and terms metadata.

```{r catalogue}
library(readfiscalnz)

releases <- list_nz_fiscal_releases()
stopifnot(
  is.data.frame(releases),
  nrow(releases) == 6L,
  all(nchar(releases$expected_sha256) == 64L)
)

releases[c(
  "release_id", "family", "status", "file_name"
)]
```

Choose a reader based on the question rather than on the release count:

* `read_nz_hfi()` selects long-run annual fiscal aggregates by named workbook
  sheet and returns `period_end`, accounting regimes, and restatement context.
* `read_nz_tax_outturn()` selects monthly revenue, receipts, or both and
  returns `date`, consolidation scope, and the tax-write-off regime.
* `read_nz_monthly_financials()` selects one or more of six statement tables
  from the February 2026 release and retains annual/YTD and actual/forecast
  roles.
* `read_nz_efu()` selects fiscal, economic, or key-indicator sheets from a
  chosen publication and retains its vintage, forecast horizon, source units,
  and actual/forecast labels.

The catalogue focuses on reviewed release identities and mapped workbook
surfaces. New publications and changed workbook layouts enter the supported
set through a catalogue and parser review.

## Retrieve and chart a time series

**Input used below:** the installed file is a derived, 32-row canonical CSV
subset of official HFI Core Crown Expenses observations for 1994--2025, not the
original Treasury XLSX. The values are unchanged from the byte-pinned workbook.
The local snapshot keeps documentation offline while exercising the public
reader, schema validation, cache, and provenance path; the live route later in
this article retrieves the original workbook.

```{r chart-data}
snapshot <- system.file(
  "extdata", "hfi-core-crown-expenses-official.csv",
  package = "readfiscalnz",
  mustWork = TRUE
)

hfi_release <- releases[
  releases$release_id == "hfi-1972-2025",
  c("release_id", "family", "status", "issue_date")
]

hfi_expenses <- read_nz_hfi(
  release_id = hfi_release$release_id[[1L]],
  file = snapshot,
  revision = "as_published",
  sheets = "Spending",
  cache_dir = cache
)

chart_data <- hfi_expenses[
  hfi_expenses$series == "Core Crown Expenses" &
    hfi_expenses$measure == "level",
  c("period_end", "value")
]
chart_data <- chart_data[
  order(chart_data$period_end),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
row.names(chart_data) <- NULL

utils::head(chart_data, 3L)
```

The filtered data contain one published level series, so the plot uses the
returned `period_end` and numeric `value` fields directly. HFI spans reporting
regime changes; retain `regime_id` and `comparability_note` from the full reader
output when interpreting changes across those boundaries. `ggplot2` remains a
suggested package and is checked before plotting.

```{r retrieve-chart-series, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.8, out.width='100%', fig.alt='Line chart of official New Zealand Core Crown expenses from 1994 to 2025.'}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    chart_data,
    ggplot2::aes(x = period_end, y = value)
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Core Crown expenses in the HFI release",
      subtitle = "Annual published observations",
      x = "Fiscal year end",
      y = "Core Crown expenses (NZD million)",
      caption = "Source: The Treasury, Historical Fiscal Indicators 1972–2025"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}
```

`nz_fiscal_provenance(hfi_expenses)` returns the exact snapshot and source
workbook hashes, parser and schema versions, and terms metadata. The complete
record and change notice are in `inst/extdata/README.md`. The source and
attribution are
[The Treasury](https://www.treasury.govt.nz/publications/information-release/data-fiscal-time-series-historical-fiscal-indicators),
and the snapshot is provided under
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). For a live refresh,
keep the selection and plotting steps unchanged and replace the local `file`
route with the bounded live route described in
[From an official release](#from-an-official-release).

## First success: replay HFI data offline

Pass a local canonical CSV to exercise the public reader, canonical-schema
validation, provenance, and cache path without network access. The CSV is
already normalised. The cache is placed under a temporary directory so the
example does not write to a user's managed cache.

```{r first-hfi}
hfi <- read_nz_hfi(
  release_id = "hfi-1972-2025",
  file = fixture_path("hfi.csv"),
  sheets = "Spending",
  cache_dir = cache
)

stopifnot(
  inherits(hfi, c("nz_fiscal_data", "data.frame")),
  inherits(hfi$period_end, "Date"),
  is.numeric(hfi$value),
  identical(names(hfi), c(
    "year", "period_end", "section", "category", "series", "measure",
    "value", "unit", "regime_id", "fiscal_year_basis", "accounting_basis",
    "gst_treatment", "consolidation_scope", "comparability_note",
    "restatement_status"
  ))
)

hfi[c("year", "period_end", "series", "measure", "value", "regime_id")]
```

Every reader returns class `c("nz_fiscal_data", "data.frame")`. The
family-specific columns stay in a stable order; date columns are `Date`,
`value` is numeric, and the semantic columns are character. The reader keeps
source order and preserves accounting regimes, missing values, and
actual/forecast roles as explicit source semantics.

The source record is attached to the result and can be inspected without
another request:

```{r first-provenance}
provenance <- nz_fiscal_provenance(hfi)
provenance[c(
  "family", "release_id", "source_kind", "raw_size_bytes", "raw_sha256",
  "parser_version", "schema_version", "revision_policy"
)]
```

## Select a canonical series

The series catalogue creates a SHA-256 identity from structural fields such as
the accounting basis, consolidation scope, unit, fiscal regime, and
actual/forecast status. Point-level annotations remain on the observations.
This makes a change in accounting regime visible instead of accidentally
joining unlike values under the same display name.

```{r series-history}
hfi_catalogue <- nz_fiscal_series_catalogue(hfi)
hfi_catalogue[c(
  "series_id", "series", "unit", "start_date", "end_date",
  "observations", "contract_version"
)]

selected_id <- hfi_catalogue$series_id[[1L]]
hfi_history <- nz_fiscal_series_history(hfi, selected_id)

stopifnot(
  inherits(hfi_history, "nz_fiscal_data"),
  all(hfi_history$period_end == sort(hfi_history$period_end)),
  all(hfi_history$value == as.numeric(hfi_history$value))
)
hfi_history[c("period_end", "series", "value", "regime_id")]
```

For HFI, two rows with the same human-readable `series` can therefore be
different canonical series when their structural regime fields differ. Use
the `series_id` returned by `nz_fiscal_series_catalogue()` rather than
reconstructing an identity from display text.

## Read the other supported surfaces

The same offline pattern applies to the other families. These examples use
the installed fixtures and make the surface choice explicit.

```{r other-readers}
tax <- read_nz_tax_outturn(
  release_id = "tax-outturn-2026-05",
  file = fixture_path("tax.csv"),
  measure = "both",
  cache_dir = cache
)

monthly <- read_nz_monthly_financials(
  release_id = "monthly-financials-2026-02",
  file = fixture_path("monthly.csv"),
  table = "performance",
  cache_dir = cache
)

efu <- read_nz_efu(
  release_id = "befu-2026",
  file = fixture_path("efu.csv"),
  dataset = "fiscal",
  cache_dir = cache
)

stopifnot(
  identical(names(tax), c(
    "date", "fiscal_year", "measure", "accounting_basis",
    "consolidation_scope", "section", "series", "value", "unit",
    "writeoff_regime"
  )),
  identical(names(monthly), c(
    "table", "statement_sheet", "period_end", "fiscal_year", "period_kind",
    "observation", "actual_forecast", "consolidation_scope",
    "accounting_basis", "section", "series", "note", "value", "unit"
  )),
  identical(names(efu), c(
    "release_type", "forecast_vintage", "forecast_horizon", "dataset",
    "sheet", "year", "period_end", "fiscal_year_basis", "actual_forecast",
    "source_status_label", "accounting_basis", "consolidation_scope", "section",
    "series", "value", "unit", "unit_multiplier", "unit_context"
  )),
  inherits(tax$date, "Date"),
  inherits(monthly$period_end, "Date"),
  inherits(efu$period_end, "Date"),
  all(c("revenue", "receipts") %in% unique(tax$measure)),
  all(efu$release_type == "BEFU")
)

data.frame(
  family = c("tax outturn", "monthly financials", "EFU"),
  rows = c(nrow(tax), nrow(monthly), nrow(efu)),
  date_column = c("date", "period_end", "period_end")
)
```

The exact family schemas are documented on the four reader reference pages.
In compact form, the shared contract is:

| Reader | Date field | Required interpretation fields |
|---|---|---|
| `read_nz_hfi()` | `period_end` | `measure`, `unit`, `regime_id`, accounting/GST/consolidation fields |
| `read_nz_tax_outturn()` | `date` | `measure`, `accounting_basis`, `consolidation_scope`, `writeoff_regime` |
| `read_nz_monthly_financials()` | `period_end` | `table`, `period_kind`, `observation`, `actual_forecast`, `unit` |
| `read_nz_efu()` | `period_end` | release type/vintage, dataset, actual/forecast, source status, unit multiplier |

## Scope and limitations

The package focuses on the six reviewed release identities and their mapped
workbook surfaces. It preserves fiscal-year, accounting, consolidation,
write-off, unit, and forecast distinctions so users can make those analytical
choices explicitly. New releases or changed workbook layouts require a
catalogue/parser update, and downstream tools remain the appropriate place for
seasonal adjustment, forecasting, imputation, or alternative accounting
interpretations.

## From an official release

The default `file = NULL` route resolves the selected catalogue release over
HTTPS. It requires an explicit `accept_terms = TRUE` after reviewing
`nz_fiscal_terms()`; downloaded bytes are size- and signature-checked and must
match the catalogue SHA-256 before parsing. The conditional block below is
intentionally skipped during ordinary vignette builds. Set
`READFISCALNZ_LIVE=true` only in an environment where live retrieval is
desired and the source terms have been reviewed.

```{r live-equivalent}
if (identical(Sys.getenv("READFISCALNZ_LIVE"), "true")) {
  live_hfi <- read_nz_hfi(
    release_id = "hfi-1972-2025",
    accept_terms = TRUE,
    cache_dir = tempfile("readfiscalnz-live-cache-"),
    timeout_sec = 30
  )
  print(live_hfi)
}
```

`accept_terms = TRUE` gates a live download after the caller's review; it is
not persisted as a provenance field or treated as a credential or licence
grant. For offline and reproducible work, retain the source file, its SHA-256,
the release identifier, and the attached provenance together. The `Sources,
provenance, and caching` vignette covers those choices in detail.

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
unlink(cache, recursive = TRUE)
```
